[17:19] You will hear a talk on the research of the graphical symbol.

[17:24] First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.

[18:09] Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.

[18:17] Good morning, everyone.

[18:19] Today I'm going to talk about the graphical symbol.

[18:22] A graphic symbol is a written symbol that is used to represent speech, such as those

[18:29] used in the Greek alphabet.

[18:32] The term graphic symbol encompasses anything from the logographs used in Egyptian hieroglyphic

[18:38] writing to ancient Chinese pictograms.

[18:42] Early symbols were based on pictographs and ideograms before they were developed into

[18:48] logographic writing systems.

[18:51] These systems are still in use in some non-literate cultures in Africa, the Americas, and Oceania.

[19:00] Indeed, elements of pictography are still found in modern Chinese characters,

[19:05] and it is often an interesting exercise to trace the origins of some Chinese characters.

[19:12] Pictographs remain in common commercial use today as signs, instructions or statistical diagrams.

[19:21] Road signs and public toilet signs and even flat pack assembly instructions utilising pictures are considered pictographic.

[19:31] Ancient graphic writing systems provide researchers with a wealth of knowledge about past civilisations.

[19:39] In 1799, one of the most important historical discoveries was made by accident when members

[19:46] of Napoleon's expedition to Egypt found a stone in Rosetta that exhibited three different

[19:52] scripts.

[19:54] The stone, now known as the Rosetta Stone, was studied in significant depth by scholars

[20:00] and was first deciphered by Frenchman Jean-Francois Champollion in 1822.

[20:09] He was able to correctly determine the phonetic values of the symbols

[20:13] and later research has confirmed his findings.

[20:17] In many of these symbols, lines are used to portray a multitude of meanings

[20:22] and knowledge and understanding of these lines

[20:26] holds the key to comprehension of graphic writing systems.

[20:31] A key moment in the history of communication

[20:34] was the invention of the camera obscura, or camera.

[20:39] Although the concept can be traced back

[20:41] to the 5th century BC Chinese philosopher Muo Ti,

[20:45] the first photographic image was ultimately created in 1826

[20:49] by Joseph Niséfour Niséf.

[20:53] Photography, as it was later known, enables researchers to piece together and better understand history.

[21:01] Today, photography forms a huge part of everyday life and most publications contain a vast number of photographs.

[21:10] Photography is used in advertising and is now becoming a way to increase awareness of existing world issues.

[21:16] For example, animal welfare charities are increasingly using photography to advertise

[21:23] animals that are at high risk of endangerment.

[21:27] Charity workers are sometimes flown to far-flung locations to document the suffering endured

[21:33] by high-risk animals in an attempt to raise human awareness of their consumption activities

[21:39] and how they impact others.

[21:42] One recent high-profile campaign was undertaken by attaching a camera to the

[21:48] foot of a bird in order to obtain photographs of the animals in their

[21:52] natural habitats and understand how often they come into contact with human

[21:57] waste. A soon-to-be released documentary about the suffering of animals on

[22:03] Midway Island shows the full extent to which human consumption is harming

[22:08] animals thousands of miles away from us. As photography continues to progress, with

[22:19] the use of drones now becoming somewhat commonplace, we should expect more and more objects to

[22:25] be included in the future, expanding the horizon of photography ever further.

[22:31] Indeed, the downward pressure on traditional media prices means that media companies are

[22:37] being forced to get creative on how to make a profit.

[22:40] side. Many have found that the answer to this lies in advertising and companies are now

[22:46] willing to devote a large portion of their budgets to advertising in newspapers.

[22:51] By the same token, marketing has become an essential part of a company's business model,

[22:57] often meaning the success or failure of a company. As a result, much time and money

[23:04] has been pumped into the development of effective branding, with attractive packaging playing

[23:09] a large role in this.

[23:12] However, many governments are now seen to be cracking down on marketing and packaging

[23:17] in an attempt to protect consumers from being misled.

[23:21] In particular, tobacco companies are now subject to ever-increasing regulation.

[23:27] For example, in the United Kingdom, legislation is soon to pass preventing any form of branding

[23:34] or differentiation on cigarette packaging in efforts to curb the harmful effects of smoking.

[23:42] Finally, one must not forget the fundamental role that graphic writing systems have had to play in mathematics.

[23:50] Graphs, icons and diagrams often form the very basis of these branches of academia.

[23:57] Indeed, one needs to look no further than Chemistry's periodic table to see a perfect example of

[24:04] graphic writing systems in use today.
